$comment: The GNAP grant state machine, derived from RFC 9635 §1.5 and the normative requirements of §3, §4 and §5. This file is the specification the implementation is written against, not a description of it: the scenarios in crates/gnap-core/tests are generated from it. Every rule cites the requirement it comes from.

states.name: processing
states.description: The AS is deciding what the request needs. A grant request enters here on creation, on modification, and when interaction completes. It must leave this state before any response is returned.

states.name: pending
states.description: Approval from an RO, or interaction with the end user, is required. No token and no subject information may be released while here.

states.name: approved
states.description: The request has been approved and no further interaction is required. Tokens and subject information may be issued.

states.name: finalized
states.description: The request is dead and cannot be revived. Entered on revocation, on denial, or when no further processing is possible.

transitions.description: A request to the grant endpoint creates a grant request in the processing state.
Approval is required: the AS returns a continuation response and any interaction responses.
No approval is required, or access has already been fulfilled.
A timeout or an unrecoverable error ends the request.
Polling while approval is still outstanding. The response carries a fresh continuation.
Interaction has finished, whether the RO approved or denied: the AS re-evaluates the full context.
Information reached the AS outside the protocol, such as an asynchronous RO approval.
The client revokes the request, or no interaction method remains usable.
Polling while approved may issue new access tokens.
A modification request sends the grant back for re-evaluation in its new context.
A modification is also allowed while pending.
The client revokes, or the AS decides no further token or update will be accepted.

response_constraints.text: The grant request MUST be in the approved state to include this field in the response.
The grant request MUST be in the approved state to return this field in the response.
The grant request MUST be in the pending state to include this field in the response.
In the pending state the response MUST NOT contain access tokens or subject information.
In the pending state the response MUST NOT contain access tokens or subject information.
A grant request in the pending state is always associated with a continuation access token.
Once finalized, no new access tokens can be issued and no subject information returned.
Once finalized, no new access tokens can be issued and no subject information returned.
Once finalized, no interactions can take place.

guards.text: If the AS detects a client submitting an interaction reference when the request is not pending, it MUST return too_many_attempts and SHOULD finalize the request.
A grant request associated with a modification request MUST be in the approved or pending state.
Once finalized, the grant request MUST NOT be moved to any other state.
If the client does not respect the given wait period, the AS MUST return the too_fast error.

guards.condition: no continuation was offered in the previous response
guards.text: If the AS does not return a new continuation response, the client MUST NOT make an additional continuation request; if it does, the AS MUST return invalid_continuation.
The interaction reference MUST be one-time-use, to prevent interception and replay.
If one interaction start mode has completed, the AS MUST reject attempts to use the others.

invariants.text: finalized is absorbing: no transition leaves it.
No access token and no subject information is ever released while pending.
An interaction reference is consumed at most once.
A response is never emitted while processing: the state machine always settles first.
Every reachable state is reachable from the initial state, and finalized is reachable from every state.
